chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyani narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Nujayyah al-Qawwas, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:
Command your companions to restrain their tongues, abandon quarreling in religion, and strive in the worship of Allah, the Mighty and High.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kadhim (AS) advise regarding speech and religious disputes?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) advises his companions to restrain their tongues and avoid *khilaf* (disagreement) in theological matters, prioritizing *ibadah* (worship) over speculative debate. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawhid* as a matter of the heart and practice rather than mere intellectual contention, guarding against the divisions that arise from excessive *kalam* (theology). The instruction underscores the ethical dimension of monotheism, where humility in worship supersedes the pride of argumentation.
